purpose: Declarative text rules used by extract_semantic_facts.py. Humans and LLMs should grow game knowledge here instead of adding new domain rules to Python.

trigger_rules.pattern: \bWhen one or more enemy units die\b
\bWhen you recycle one or more cards?(?: to your Main Deck)?\b
\bWhen you stun one or more enemy units?\b
\bWhen you attach an Equipment to me\b

condition_rules.pattern: \bIf you paid my additional cost, you don't kill a unit this way\b
\bThe next time (?:that unit|it) would die this turn, heal it, exhaust it, and recall it instead\b
\bIf a friendly unit would die, kill this instead\. Heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it\b
\bIf I would die, kill Guardian Angel instead\. Heal me, exhaust me, and recall me\b
\bIf another unit you control here would die, if it has less Might than me, instead heal it, exhaust it, and recall it\b
\bIf a unit here would die during combat, its controller may pay (?P<cost>(?::rb_rune_[a-z]+:)+) to heal it, exhaust it, and recall it instead\b

cost_rules.pattern: \bYou may (?P<verb>pay|spend|kill|discard|recycle|exhaust) (?P<body>.+?) as an additional cost to play (?:me|this)\b
